core_obligations: Record that the property 'F is flat over S at all generic points of fibres' is preserved under strict transform and local on S, so that the successive-blowup reductions are available (proof lines 8802-8811).

Define the rank function r(u) at the generic point of the fibre X_u and prove it locally constant using the fibrewise flat-and-free statement and openness of the image of an open of X_S in S, then write U as a finite disjoint union of the level sets U_0, ..., U_c (proof lines 8814-8825).
Separate the level sets by admissible blowups using the disjoint-opens separation lemma, c - 1 times, to reduce to the case where r is constant (proof lines 8826-8834).

Reduce further, using the successive-blowup remark twice, to the case S = Spec(R) with the complement of U defined by a single nonzerodivisor f, and quote the helper lemma for the affine-space case to conclude the existence of V (proof lines 8837-8845).
proof_roadmap: Invariance and locality of the flatness-at-generic-points hypothesis (proof lines 8802-8811).
Local constancy of the fibrewise rank and separation of the level sets by blowups (proof lines 8814-8834).
Reduction to the affine one-equation case and the quoted helper computation (proof lines 8837-8845).
difficulty_reason: Under the assumptions that X -> S is affine of finite presentation and flat with geometrically integral fibres, F is of finite type and of finite presentation over U, and F is flat over S at the generic points of fibres over U, the lemma produces a U-admissible blowup S' -> S and an open V of X_{S'} whose preimage is surjective onto S' and on which the strict transform of F is finite locally free (statement lines 8781-8800). The proof is a reduction built on an invariance: the property 'flat at the generic points of the fibres' is preserved by strict transform and is local on S, so the standard successive-blowup reductions apply. The author then defines the rank function r(u) = dim_{kappa(xi_u)}(F_{xi_u} tensor kappa(xi_u)) at the generic point of the fibre over u, proves it locally constant by a fibrewise flat-and-free statement, separates the finitely many level sets U_0, ..., U_c by admissible blowups, reduces to r constant, and finally reduces to S affine with the complement of U cut out by a single nonzerodivisor, where the concluding case is quoted from the affine-space helper lemma (proof lines 8802-8846). The locally-constant-rank argument and the use of disjoint-union blowups to separate the level sets are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
